summary.name: LightTable
summary.one_liner: LightTable is a free, open-source desktop photo editor for macOS, Windows, and Linux that focuses on realistic film stock simulation built on Spektrafilm.
use_cases: simulate film stock looks on digital photos
switch from Lightroom Classic and import catalog
edit RAW photos with film-style color and grain
prepare images for screen or print with soft proofing
merge photos into HDR, panoramas, or focus stacks
automate photo editing via command line tools
summary.what_it_does: LightTable is a desktop digital darkroom with a Rust core and GPU-accelerated rendering. Its film simulation is built on Spektrafilm and offers 23 film stocks, physical grain scaled by stock and format, and print paper, exposure, preflash, and filtration controls. It also includes halation, diffusion, glare, scan softness, and sharpening. Standard editing covers curves, color grading, masks, healing, cloning, lens correction via Lensfun profiles, RAW processing for 1,275 cameras, and HDR, panorama, and focus stacking. It can import Lightroom Classic catalogs and XMP or .lrtemplate presets, reporting which settings were converted or skipped.
notable: Film simulation built on Spektrafilm with 23 film stocks
Rust core with GPU-driven rendering and a comprehensive CLI
Imports Lightroom Classic catalogs and presets, reporting skipped settings
On Mac, optional AI subject recognition using local models
caveats: The macOS build only works on Apple silicon; Intel Macs are not supported
macOS build requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later
For cloud-based Lightroom, originals must be exported to files first
